definitions.explanation: A collection of various items packed together in one box or package, typically food items such as sweets, cookies, or fruits. Very common as gifts in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: クッキーの{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought an assortment of cookies.

examples.japanese: お{歳暮|せいぼ}にフルーツの{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせを{贈|おく}った。
examples.english: I sent a fruit assortment as a year-end gift.

examples.japanese: この{和菓子|わがし}の{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせは{手土産|てみやげ}にぴったりだ。
examples.english: This assortment of Japanese sweets is perfect as a gift to bring when visiting.

notes:
USAGE:
{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ is extremely common in the context of gift-giving and shopping. Japanese gift culture relies heavily on boxed assortments of food items. The word comes from {詰|つ}める (to pack) and {合|あ}わせる (to combine), literally meaning items packed together. It almost always refers to food items.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{菓子|かし}の{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ: assortment of sweets
- フルーツの{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ: fruit assortment
- {詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせセット: assortment set
- {詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせギフト: assortment gift box
